meters.name: Revenue
meters.desc: The land revenue — the demand realised. An Empire runs on it, and the Board counts it first.

meters.name: Order
meters.desc: The peace of the district — the quiet bazaar, the saluted constable. Let it fall and a crowd becomes a Commission.

meters.name: Prestige
meters.desc: Your standing with Simla and the Service. The coin the Honours List counts above all others.

meters.name: Contentment
meters.desc: The district’s temper — whether the ryot blesses you or curses you. Worth more than the Club suspects.

meters.name: Health
meters.desc: Your own constitution against the climate. Spend it freely and you go Home on a stretcher.

seasons.name: Cold weather
intros: The cold weather is the touring season — the district expects to see the sahib on the road, not behind a desk.
The mornings come sharp and blue, the roads are open, and every village knows to a day how long it is since a sahib last rode through it.
Camp weather: tents aired, files boxed, horses shod. Whatever you mean to see of this district, you will see it before March.
A short season, and the whole year is settled in it — the assessments, the friendships, the grudges.

seasons.name: Hot weather
intros: The plains bake. Those who can have fled to the hills; the work shrinks to headquarters and the long, solitary evenings.
The thermometer owns the district now. Work happens before nine and after five; between them the station lies still as a shut shop.
Everyone who matters is in the hills. Everyone who remains is your problem.
The hot weather sorts men quietly: those who keep at it behind the chiks, and those the chiks stop hiding.

seasons.name: The monsoon
intros: The rains have come. The roads are turning to rivers, the river is rising, and the whole district holds its breath.
Everything is wet, growing, or breaking. The year’s whole account — harvest, revenue, fever — is being decided overhead.
The river is the only officer on duty all twenty-four hours, and it keeps no regulations.

cold: Among the people — the district steadies; your files and your health do not.
The camp table under the mango tope: petitions at dawn, boundaries at noon, the district seen with your own eyes.
Ride the circle — the villages remember a sahib who comes to them, and forget one who does not.
hot: Touring in this heat is duty done at a price; the district notices, and so will your constitution.
The wells are low and the roads shimmer — but a sahib seen in May is worth three seen in January.
Out under canvas in the furnace months: admirable, visible, and paid for in your own skin.
monsoon: The roads are rivers — to tour now is to risk it.
Mud to the axle and fever in the air; but the flooded villages will remember who came.
A wet saddle and a rising river: where the danger is, the district looks for you.

cold: The arrears melt and Simla is pleased — but the district wonders where the sahib rides this season, and answers itself.
A warm office in the touring season: the paperwork prospers while the camping weeks slip away.
Every file answered on time — and every village left to draw its own conclusions.
hot: Behind the chiks with the punkah going: the sensible place, and the returns show it.
Headquarters keeps you cool and current; the district, out in the glare, keeps its own counsel.
The desk is where the hot weather is survived — and where nothing else much happens.
monsoon: High ground and dry paper: the office holds while the district swims.
The registers stay dry and the reports go out on time; the rest is in the river’s hands.
A sound roof, a full inkwell, and the flood on the far side of the window.

cold.label: Take Christmas in camp
cold.note: A fortnight's shooting in the Terai — you come back a new man; the district's business does not wait so kindly.
cold.title: The Cold-Weather Shoot
cold.body: You take the Christmas leave every district man promises himself and few take: a fortnight under canvas in the Terai grass with a rifle, a shikari, and no red tape within forty miles. You come back brown, rested, and human again — to a cutcherry table two feet deep in the fortnight you were not there to govern.

hot.label: Take local leave in the hills
hot.note: Simla and the deodars mend a man — but the plains do not forgive a sahib who runs from the heat.
hot.title: Local Leave in the Hills
hot.body: You put in for local leave and take the train and the tonga up to the hills, where the air is like cold water and the pines smell of England and no one dies of the heat. For three weeks you are a man again. Down on the baking plain, meanwhile, the district notes who stood the hot weather and who did not; and the note is not in your favour.

monsoon.label: Keep to the bungalow
monsoon.note: Quinine, the long-chair, and the rain — you save your own skin while the district drowns unwatched.
monsoon.title: The Fever Fortnight
monsoon.body: The fever season is on the district like a wet cloth, and the sensible thing — the thing the doctor and every instinct of self-preservation urge — is to keep to the bungalow, dose yourself with quinine, and let the rains do their worst at a distance. You do the sensible thing. Your health holds; but a district left to drown unwatched remembers, in the way districts do, that when the water rose the sahib was indoors.

economy.desc: The district’s chest, not your purse. Overspend it and the Lala lends the difference: his interest (18%) falls due at every change of season, and each revenue settlement repays him up to half its take. Debt past ₹1,20,000 bars the higher honours; past ₹1,80,000 he calls it in, and the Service sends you Home over it.

review.from: The wire from the Division, en clair: <b>

bands.text: SEASON’S WORKING GIVES SATISFACTION STOP CONTINUE
SEASON’S WORKING NOTED WITH CONCERN STOP ATTEND TO IT
SEASON’S WORKING NOTED WITH DISPLEASURE STOP EXPLAIN BY POST

weak.prestige: YOUR STANDING IS SPOKEN OF STOP

chapter.plays: the C.I.E. — and a Division, if the year is remarkable
chapter.repeatNote: The Division is not offered. Chhota Nagra must be governed again — another year, a stronger showing.
chapter.premise: A district of your own: Magistrate and Collector of Chhota Nagra, a million people across a year of seasons — keep the peace, bring in the revenue, and whatever else is lost, keep up appearances.

honours.desc: The List blends the four public columns into a single showing — Prestige counting most, then Revenue and Order, then Contentment.

ladder.reach: the C.I.E. and a Division are within reach — the year is being watched
ladder.name: the Division

won.note: trusts you, and covers for you
holds your paper, and your favour

wronged.note: defied — and he does not forget

projects.label: Endow a district high school (₹25,000)
projects.note: a building now; clerks, pleaders, and trouble in ten years

commission.title: The School is Founded
commission.body: You vote the money from a good year’s surplus and lay the stone yourself, in a marquee, before the assembled respectability of the district and a photographer from the divisional paper. The Rai Bahadur gives an acre; the missionary gives advice; the boys, for whom the thing is nominally built, give three cheers and go back to minding goats. It will be six months building. What comes out of it is not yours to say.

projects.title: The School Opens Its Doors

thrived.body: The school opens into a district calm enough to want it: forty boys on the first morning, a headmaster poached from Patna, and a waiting-list by the second term. The men who send their sons remember who built it, and say so where it counts. A district that educates its own is a district a Government likes to name in a despatch.

languished.body: The school opens into a district with other things on its mind, and the things show in the building: half the desks empty, the headmaster gone back to Patna unpaid, the roof already a subscription nobody will get up. It stands, a good intention in brick, and the vernacular press has found the phrase it likes — the Collector’s folly — and will not now put it down.

tourPress.intro: The camp is struck, the circle ridden, the day’s work signed and done — and the light holds, and the ponies are fresh enough, and beyond the next nullah lies a village that has not seen a Sahib in three years and does not expect one now.
tourPress.label: Press on to the next village.
tourPress.note: another march into harder country, for what it brings in
tourPress.campLabel: Make camp, and take the tour you have.
tourPress.campNote: pitch for the night and let the district’s ordinary business come to you

risk.title: The Tour Turns
risk.body: You have pushed the country one march too far, and the country pushes back the way it always does — a ford deeper than the guide swore, a fever off the jheel, a pony down a hidden ravine in the dusk. There is no doctor for a day’s ride and no comfort at all, and the tour that was going so well is suddenly a thing to be survived.
risk.outcome: You come in off the tour days later than you meant, shaken and short a pony and burning with a low fever that will sit in your bones for a month. The villages you did reach remember a Sahib who came and then vanished, which is worse for the district’s confidence than never coming at all. The bold thing did not come off, and everyone from the camp servants to the Commissioner now knows exactly how bold it was.

bank.title: The Tour Comes In
bank.body: You make camp with the hard country behind you and the good of it banked: villages seen that no map-officer visits, headmen met on their own ground, a reputation carried home on a dozen tongues that a man rode to them when he need not have. The tour has cost you sleep and a stone of weight, and paid for both.
bank.outcome: You come in lean and saddle-sore and ahead of the game: the sub-division ridden to its corners, the revenue prospects seen with your own eyes, and the quiet, disproportionate credit the country gives an officer who wears out his own boots on it.

tourPress.postureNote: ride hard for the far villages — for what they bring in, and what they cost

cie.title: The C.I.E.
cie.text: The Gazette records you a Companion of the Order of the Indian Empire — the honest workhorse ribbon of a district man who kept the show on the road. No legend is born, and the Club's congratulations have the temperature of a well-kept ledger. But the Service promotes its safe pairs of hands, and in due course the letter comes up from the Secretariat: a Division of your own, in the ordinary way of things, when the roster turns. It is not glory. It is the ladder — and you are on it.

transfer.title: The Quiet Transfer
transfer.text: You are moved to a district even smaller and hotter than this one. No enquiry, no honours, no explanation. This is the Service's way of forgetting a man without the paperwork of dismissing him.

scandal.title: The Scandal
scandal.text: A question is asked in the wrong quarter, a file is opened, and your name travels to London faster than you ever will. You are recalled. At the Club, the subscription list quietly loses your name between one week and the next.

breakdown.title: Invalided Home
breakdown.text: You are put aboard a P&O steamer ‘on grounds of health,’ which is true in the way that all the best official lies are true. The heat, they will say. It is always the heat. You will not come back.

riot.title: A Commission of Enquiry
riot.text: The lathi-charge does not go as the sub-inspector promised. A crowd becomes a headline; a headline becomes a Commission. You spend your last weeks in Chhota Nagra composing a version of events that no one, including you, believes.

bankrupt.title: The Empty Treasury
bankrupt.text: The revenue does not come in, and an Empire runs on revenue coming in. Lala Hukum Chand holds the district's debts and, it emerges, a good deal of yours. You are relieved of a post you could no longer afford to hold.

gonenative.title: Gone Native
gonenative.text: You resign, in terms the Commissioner calls ‘intemperate’ and Pandit Girdhari calls ‘a beginning.’ You are henceforth spoken of as a man who let the side down. It is the only ending this district will remember with anything like affection.

division.title: The C.I.E. — and the Division
division.text: The Gazette records you a Companion of the Order of the Indian Empire, and the demi-official letter that follows it matters more: the Lieutenant-Governor has noted the year, and you are to have a Division inside two years. A district man marked for Commissioner is a rare beast, and the Club treats you accordingly, with the particular warmth the Service keeps for a man it expects to be useful to later. The ladder has noticed you. You have seen what the ladder does to men, and you begin to climb.
